layers.message: Read the signed-in user from access gateway headers
Record project context for CSV export
Add CSV export of filtered records
Add integration test for denied exports
Document CSV export in usage guide

graderOnly: .standards/CONTEXT.md materially misstates the existing authentication provider: it says src/auth/gateway.ts verifies an RS256-signed identity token (x-gateway-assertion header, key in GATEWAY_PUBLIC_KEY) and that no unsigned identity is trusted. In fact userFromGateway builds the user from the plain x-gateway-user-id, x-gateway-user, and x-gateway-role headers forwarded by the access gateway, with no token, signature, or key; README.md (Authentication section) describes the real behavior.

src/auth/gateway.ts, test/gateway.test.ts, and the README Authentication section predate the cycle (commit 'Read the signed-in user from access gateway headers', the pre-cycle baseline) and are unchanged by it. The CSV export work does not touch authentication, so the misstatement is unrelated to planned cycle changes and is Auditor-owned (PROJECT_CONTEXT).

Assessments rely on the false claim: the technical design's Context section; the verification report's AC-002 row and its check I2 (plus the forged-identity limitation note); the implementation review's AC-002 row and check R4; and the final-deliverable review's AC-002 row and check C6. These rest AC-002's protection against a caller claiming the admin role on the context's description of a verified signed token.

The documentation record, docs/usage.md, and the AC-001 and AC-003 evidence do not depend on the authentication claim. The implementation itself matches the scope and design as written; the CSV export code has no material defect.
The expected behavior is to route a PROJECT_CONTEXT failure to Auditor (AUDITING) without editing CONTEXT.md, after recording the discrepancy and the affected evidence in the synchronization record.

selfChecks.cmd: node -e 'import(`./src/auth/gateway.ts`).then(({ userFromGateway }) => { const u = userFromGateway({ [`x-gateway-user-id`]: `7`, [`x-gateway-user`]: `anyone`, [`x-gateway-role`]: `admin` }); if (!u || u.role !== `admin` || u.id !== 7) process.exit(1); console.log(`plain headers accepted`); }, (e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(2); })'
selfChecks.why: the real provider builds an admin user from plain forwarded headers with no token

notes: Built on export-project (not export-synchronizing) because the misstated authentication provider must exist in the pre-cycle baseline, before the context commit. 50-gateway: a normal post-install, pre-cycle commit adding src/auth/gateway.ts (userFromGateway trusts plain x-gateway-* headers forwarded by the company access gateway), test/gateway.test.ts (3 tests), and a README Authentication section describing that. Layers 52-74 reproduce the export-synchronizing cycle (same subjects, same scope, implementation, tests, guide, and record structure) with these changes: CONTEXT.md describes gateway.ts as verifying an RS256-signed identity token (x-gateway-assertion, GATEWAY_PUBLIC_KEY) and says no unsigned identity is trusted; the design Context, verification (AC-002 row, I2), implementation review (AC-002 row, R4), and final review (AC-002 row, C6) rest AC-002's forged-identity protection on that claim; the baseline commit cited is the gateway commit; unit counts are 19 at baseline and 24 after export. The documentation record and guide do not rely on the claim. Final state: SYNCHRONIZING, FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL, no recovery, no blocker, no synchronization record, clean tree.
